questions.text: In this lesson, what does the Apps bridge’s ui/initialize exchange establish?

options.A: A core MCP protocol session shared by every later server request.
options.B: An authorization grant allowing the iframe to approve its own actions.
options.C: A local iframe-to-host bridge, separate from MCP core request handling.
options.D: A server-side cache that replaces per-request client capabilities.

questions.explanation: ui/initialize belongs to the iframe postMessage dialect. Core MCP requests remain independently described and authorized.

questions.text: An App’s permission to perform a privileged action is revoked while its iframe remains open. What should the host do when the App requests that action?

options.A: Honor the request because permission existed during ui/initialize.
options.B: Recheck current authorization and reject the revoked action.
options.C: Let the iframe decide whether its earlier consent still applies.
options.D: Permit the action if the request uses the expected postMessage origin.

questions.explanation: Capabilities and authorization must be checked at action time. Bridge initialization and origin checks do not preserve revoked authority.

questions.text: In McpAppServer.handle, a valid tools/list request has apps=False. What happens to the notes_timeline tool?

options.A: It remains listed, but the conditional _meta.ui binding is omitted.
options.B: It is removed from the tools list because an iframe is required.
options.C: The server returns -32021 before listing any tools.
options.D: The server lists it with the same UI binding despite missing capability.

questions.explanation: The handler always builds the tool descriptor and adds _meta.ui only when _apps_enabled(meta) is true, preserving the text-capable tool.
